description: Nous sommes une équipe d'étudiants en informatique basés au Bénin, passionnés par l'IA, la Data Science, la cybersécurité et le développement web/logiciel. Pour le NASA Space Apps 2026, notre objectif est de transformer les données ouvertes de la NASA en une solution concrète et utile. Notre noyau est prêt : si tu as des compétences en design UI/UX ou analyse de données, rejoins-nous !

details:
What it does and how it works
ASTRO-PULSE is an offline health console for astronauts on long-duration missions such as Mars. In the target system, a smartwatch worn by each astronaut continuously streams vital signs (heart rate, HRV, blood pressure, sleep) to ASTRO-PULSE, alongside other wearable sensors (like the Canadian Space Agency's Bio-Monitor), dosimeters and onboard exercise devices. ASTRO-PULSE turns this data into decisions. It tracks four risk areas: cardiovascular (heart rate, HRV, blood pressure), bone and muscle (ARED exercise minutes, bone density), radiation and immunity (daily and cumulative dose, CRP inflammation marker) and behavior (sleep, mood, focus, fatigue). Each value is compared to the astronaut's own baseline (mean and standard deviation of previous sols), not just fixed thresholds. Cross-factor rules based on NASA HRP risk thresholds detect patterns that matter more together than alone: a solar particle event with rising inflammation, short sleep with low HRV, missed exercise with bone loss. For each alert, the app shows a 7-day projection if nothing is done and an immediate action protocol: move to the storm shelter, electrolyte hydration, 4-7-8 breathing, ARED session, protected sleep window, crew check-in.

Data
Three simulated 30-sol mission scenarios (nominal, solar storm, isolation) calibrated on published references (MSL RAD 1.84 mSv/day, NASA HRP bone loss of 1 to 1.5% per month, 60 min ARED, 8 h sleep). Nine public datasets: NASA bed-rest analog studies (AGBRESA, BRSM neurology, immunity, renal, pharmacology), Apollo nutrition records and PMData wearable wellness data. In the current prototype, smartwatch data comes in through an Apple Health export or a CSV file; a direct Bluetooth link to the watch is the next step.

Benefits and impact
Earth can be up to 20 minutes away on Mars. ASTRO-PULSE lets crews detect health drift early and act autonomously, without waiting for a ground physician. Continuous smartwatch monitoring means problems are caught between medical checks, not after. It supports crew autonomy and can also serve analog missions and remote settings on Earth.

Tools
React, TypeScript, Vite, deployed on Vercel. Cursor as our development environment. Hardware: designed for consumer and space-grade smartwatches and wearables; the prototype runs in any browser, fully client-side.

Creativity
Instead of building another sensor, we built the decision layer on top of existing ones, starting with the smartwatch every crew member can wear. It combines signals across body systems, personalizes alerts to each astronaut and turns alerts into concrete steps a crew can follow immediately.

Factors considered
Communication delay and offline operation, data privacy (everything stays local, on board), the limits of small analog datasets, explainability (every alert shows which values triggered it), and safety: it supports the crew and flight surgeons but is not a medical device.
